title: Accountability Ledger Event Contract
description: Machine-checkable form of ONE line in the hash-chained, append-only ACCOUNTABILITY LEDGER (Phase 0.2 — .tess/state/ledger/<YYYY-MM>.<origin>.jsonl). The 'who did what, when, who's holding it' audit trail Xavier's re-aimed vision calls for, sibling to task.schema.json (which tracks the CURRENT state of a task; this schema tracks the immutable HISTORY of events that produced it). Ported from Hermes' kanban design's task_events audit (kb/wiki/synthesis/2026-07-19-hermes-codebase-fork-study.md). `tessctl log append` dogfood-validates every event against THIS schema (via the in-memory dict, before it is ever written to a shard — `_ledger_self_validate_or_raise`) — same discipline as `_self_validate_or_raise` for mission/task records, adapted to a value that is appended rather than a file that is replaced. Each shard's own hash chain detects a non-re-chained edit to an already-appended line, a removed/reordered line, and (Phase 0.2 hardening, Cyra M1) — via the per-event `seq` below cross-checked against the shard's own `.tip` sidecar and the ledger-wide `.registry.json` — a removed TAIL line or a deleted whole shard (`tessctl log verify`): `hash = sha256(prev_hash + canonical_json(event minus hash))`, `prev_hash` of the first event in a shard is 64 zero hex chars (genesis). SCOPE (Cyra L1, PR #113 review): this is an UNSIGNED hash chain. It detects accidental or naive tampering — an edit that does not also re-chain every hash after it — NOT a determined adversary with filesystem write access who recomputes the ENTIRE downstream chain to match a shortened or altered history (a `verify` pass over such a fully-and-consistently re-chained forgery would still report OK). It is not a cryptographic signature, carries no signer identity, and makes no non-repudiation claim; see docs/STATE_LAYER.md's trust-boundary note.

ts.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp ('...Z' suffix) this event was appended — NOT necessarily when the underlying action started (e.g. a `claim` event's `ts` is append time; the task record's own `claim.claimed_at` is the authoritative claim-start time).

actor.description: Who/what produced this event — the cross-harness accountability identity: which harness, optionally which model/session/persona.

event.description: Event classification. `task_transition` covers any tracked change to a task record via `tessctl tasks new|set` (including creation itself, logged as '(none) -> <initial status>'); `claim`/`heartbeat`/`release`/`completed`/`crashed`/`reclaimed` are `tessctl tasks claim|release`'s own five-way claim-lifecycle classification (Hermes' 'claimed/completed/crashed/reclaimed' vocabulary, verbatim); `dispatch`/`session_open`/`session_close` are broader harness-lifecycle bookkeeping events logged directly via `tessctl log append`, not tied to any one task.

refs.description: What this event refers to. `_lint_ledger_event` requires `refs.task` to be non-null for every task-scoped event class (`task_transition`, `claim`, `heartbeat`, `release`, `completed`, `crashed`, `reclaimed`) — a relational rule plain JSON Schema cannot express against a sibling field's own value.

summary.description: Human-readable one-line description of what happened (e.g. 'status: backlog -> in_progress', 'claimed by ada-host:4821:9c1e...'). Never empty — an empty summary carries no accountability information, the same rule task.schema.json's Note.text already applies.

seq.description: Monotonic, gapless, PER-SHARD sequence number — 0 for the first event ever appended to a shard, incrementing by exactly 1 for every subsequent event in THAT SAME shard (independent of every other shard's own seq, same per-shard scoping as `prev_hash`). Phase 0.2 hardening (Cyra M1, PR #113 review): a pure `prev_hash` chain walk cannot detect a REMOVED TAIL line — every remaining line's own `prev_hash` link to its predecessor stays internally consistent, the file just 'ends early.' `tessctl log verify` cross-checks the tail `seq` (and event count, and tip `hash`) it actually finds against the shard's own co-located `.tip` sidecar and the ledger-wide `.registry.json`, so a removed tail line (count/seq lower than recorded) or a deleted whole shard (registered but absent on disk) is DETECTED rather than silently reported OK.

prev_hash.description: The `hash` of the immediately preceding event IN THIS SAME SHARD (64 zero hex chars — genesis — for the first event ever appended to a shard). Chains are per-shard, NOT global: shards are sharded per calendar month AND per writer origin specifically so two machines/harnesses writing concurrently never contend on, or need to interleave into, the SAME chain (see .tess/bin/tessctl's TASK LEDGER region header).

hash.description: sha256(`prev_hash` + compact key-sorted JSON of this event, including `seq`, with the `hash` key itself removed) — the same 'canonical bytes minus the field being computed' construction `verdict_canonical_bytes`/`signoff_canonical_bytes` already use elsewhere in this engine, applied here to build a hash CHAIN, not a signature — there is no private key and no signer identity bound to this value (Cyra L1, PR #113 review). `tessctl log verify` recomputes this for every line and compares; any mismatch, OR any `prev_hash` that does not equal the prior line's `hash`, is reported as tamper. See this schema's top-level description for the precise (and deliberately narrower than 'tamper-evident') threat-model scope this mechanism actually covers.

model.description: Which model was driving the harness, if known/relevant.

session.description: The harness session id, if the caller supplied one.

persona.description: Which named persona/agent (e.g. 'Ada') was acting, if relevant.

task.description: Task id this event refers to, or null for a task-independent event (dispatch/session_open/session_close).

mission.description: Mission id this event refers to, or null.

$comment: Minimal-validator keyword subset supported by tessctl validate: type, enum, const, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, minItems, maxItems, minLength, maxLength, pattern, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, if/then/else, oneOf, anyOf, allOf, contains, $ref, $defs.
